The framework chooses different curricula through an adaptive multi-curricula scheduler formulated under reinforcement learning [E2]. The scheduler acts as a policy that interacts with the dialogue model to acquire its current learning status, using the model's performance on the validation set to guide scheduling [E2]. It then selects a scheduling action, and the current mini-batch of training samples is drawn according to that action [E2]. After the dialogue model trains on that mini-batch, it reaches a new learning status, so the scheduler can adjust the curriculum again at the next step [E2]. This process is driven by a reward signal that measures how well the current model performs; actions that improve performance receive positive reward, which encourages the framework to automatically favor better curricula as learning evolves [E2].

frontier_answer: Frege's holistic and functional approach to meaning states that a word has meaning only in the context of a sentence [E1]. It also holds that the role or meaning contribution of an expression depends on its context and function in use; for example, the number "5" plays different roles in "5 is a prime number" and "there are 5 cows on the meadow" [E4].

According to the evidence, Frege's approach as interpreted here is related to the general distributional hypothesis by sharing the same holistic view of meaning: both are described as approaches in which the meaning of the whole determines the meaning of the parts [E3]. The evidence characterizes holism as the idea that language or theory is the primary vehicle of meaning, and that the meanings of smaller units are derived from that whole [E1]. It also states that words have meaning in sentences and sentences in a language, reinforcing this whole-to-part orientation [E4]. In the AI connection, the paper says this implicit holistic component is central to the quality of Skip-gram representations, tying the distributional hypothesis to that Fregean-style holistic perspective [E2].

Dialogue is guided by a finite state machine that constrains what can be said or done at each step. The FSM tracks the current dialogue state and only offers suitable, relevant transitions based on the interaction context, world state, and history [E2]. In practice, this means Wizards are limited to relevant and plausible dialogue options rather than acting freely [E3]. The system also enforces procedural checkpoints: some transitions require an Operator answer or authorization, and the dialogue state is locked until that condition is satisfied [E5]. Because robot-control commands are themselves FSM transitions, procedural actions are likewise constrained by the state machine [E5].

The dialogue is guided primarily by a finite-state machine that constrains the conversation to predefined paths and treats robot-control commands as explicit state transitions, which limits what actions can be taken through dialogue [E2]. In addition, certain transitions cannot proceed unless the Operator provides the required answer or authorization; the system locks the dialogue state until that condition is satisfied [E2]. Participants also receive role-specific instructions in text and video on how to play and how to select dialogues and robots, which further steers interaction toward the intended procedures [E1].

frontier_answer: Masked document generation (MDG) is a seq2seq pre-training task in STEP where the model learns to recover a document after masking a span of tokens, i.e., to restore the masked document to its original form [E1][E2]. Concretely, for a document token sequence X, the method samples a span length l uniformly from U(a,b) and a start position k uniformly from U(1, |X|-l+1), and masks the span M=(x_k, x_{k+1}, ..., x_{k+l-1}) [E1].

Masked document generation is a pre-training task in which a document subsequence is masked to form a corrupted document, and the model is trained on pairs of the masked document and the original document. In the masked subsequence, each token is either replaced with [MASK], replaced with a random token, or left unchanged [E2]. The paper specifies the proportions as 80% [MASK], 10% random token, and 10% unchanged [E2].

The most helpful of the three pretraining tasks is SR (sentence reordering). The paper states that SR works slightly better than NSG and MDG, and with more pre-training data it consistently achieves the highest ROUGE-2; accordingly, the authors conclude that SR is the most effective task. [E2]

frontier_answer: Morphological analysis and morphological inflection differ in what they take as input and what they produce as output. Morphological analysis starts from a given word and produces its morphosyntactic description or sequence of morphological tags [E1]. Morphological inflection, by contrast, starts from a lemma together with a set of morphological tags and produces the corresponding inflected word form [E2]. So, analysis is essentially word-form-to-tags, while inflection is lemma-plus-tags-to-word-form [E1][E2].
